meta.parties: Uduma Levvai v. Mayatin Vava Et Al

rules.statement: A donation inter vivos is irrevocable once it is accepted, and the donee has a present right to the thing donated, with possession postponed until the donor's death.
rules.supporting_quote: "It is manifest that there are no words in this deed from which it may be inferred that the donor had any intention to revoke it and to take back what was gifted at any time before his death. But that really makes no difference one way or another in view of the attitude which both the parties to it took up at its execution. A donation inter vivos is in its nature irrevocable once it is accepted; and in that respect it differs from a last will, which the testator may revoke at any time he likes."
